event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: TSN’s 2023-11-13 10-K frames COVID-19 as a still-material, multi-faceted threat that first struck in early-2020 and continues to reverberate through its labour force, supply chain, legal exposure, consumer-demand mix and cost base.  The narrative blends backward-looking evidence (e.g., actual shutdowns, cost inflation, lawsuits and demand shifts) with forward-looking warnings about variants, future pandemics and unpredictable government actions.  Most disclosures are specific to the company’s operations—higher safety costs, raw-material inflation, pending litigation, supply-chain bottlenecks—yet remain largely unquantified.  Because the filing date is only about 3 ¾ years after the WHO pandemic declaration, the Time-Decay Principle still permits elevated severity scores (upper-mid single digits) though some fading from peak-crisis levels is appropriate.  Overall, the risk is assessed as high but no longer catastrophic: the pandemic has already hurt margins and generated litigation, while its trajectory (variants, policy responses, consumer behaviour) remains highly uncertain and could further erode profitability, liquidity and strategic flexibility.

evidence_list.snippet: Global pandemics have had, and may in the future have, an adverse impact on our business and operations.

components.reason: Acknowledges historical and future adverse impact from pandemics.
Applies to entire business and operations (broad scope).
Event is recent (<4 yrs) so time-decay still elevates relevance.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic but clear statement that pandemics already hurt TSN and can do so again; recent timeframe justifies a moderate-high score.

evidence_list.snippet: Specifically, the COVID-19 pandemic negatively affected many parts of our business and operations, and the sustained, continuing impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic (including indirect effects from the immediate impacts of the pandemic) remain difficult to predict, including, but not limited to, the duration and spread of additional variants, the efficacy of vaccines against new variants and the speed at which normal economic and operating conditions can resume.

components.reason: Directly links negative effects to COVID-19 across ‘many parts’ of the business.
Highlights ongoing, unpredictable nature of variants and recovery speed.
Wide operational scope increases materiality.
Lack of quantification slightly tempers severity.
Recency (<4 yrs) sustains high relevance.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Lists concrete continuing uncertainties and broad operational reach, warranting a high score despite no dollar figures.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced, and expect to continue to experience, an increase in operating costs in connection with higher costs associated with protecting the health and safety of team members.

components.reason: Confirms actual cost increases already incurred.
Forecasts future cost pressure (‘expect to continue’).
Targets labour-safety spending, a critical expense driver.
No quantification of magnitude.
Event window still recent.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Demonstrates realised and ongoing cost inflation tied to COVID-19; specificity on operating costs yields a solid risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: If a significant percentage of our workforce is unable to work, including because of illness, this could have an adverse effect on our operations and results of operations.

components.reason: Identifies potential large-scale labour disruption due to illness.
Connects directly to operational and financial impact.
Risk is hypothetical (contingent).
Still within recent pandemic period.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights a plausible but not yet realised threat to capacity; lower immediacy keeps score moderate.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, certain of our team members who claim to have tested positive for COVID-19, or their family members, have filed lawsuits seeking compensatory and punitive damages for wrongful death and personal injury claims in several states, and additional team members or family members of team members may assert similar claims as new COVID-19 variants, other contagions or if a new global pandemic arises.

components.reason: Reports actual litigation already filed, showing realized legal exposure.
Mentions possibility of additional claims, expanding future liability.
Potential for significant compensatory and punitive damages.
Recent timeframe heightens relevance.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete lawsuits plus prospect of more claims drive a high severity score tied to tangible financial risk.

evidence_list.snippet: We have also experienced, and expect to continue to experience, disruption and volatility in our supply chain, which has resulted, and may continue to result, in increased costs for certain raw materials, packaging materials and transportation costs.

components.reason: Discloses actual supply-chain disruption and cost increases.
Projects continuation of these pressures (forward-looking).
Covers multiple cost categories (raw materials, packaging, transport).
No dollar quantification.
Recency keeps risk elevated.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Demonstrated ongoing supply-chain cost inflation supports a strong, above-average risk rating.

evidence_list.snippet: Other supply chain risks associated with a global pandemic include but are not limited to shutdowns or reduced operations at our suppliers’ facilities, the continued inability of some of our contract producers to manage their livestock, supply chain disruptions for feed grains, changes in consumer orders due to shifting consumer patterns, changes in livestock and protein market prices, and additional disruptions in logistics or the distribution chain for our products, the occurrence of any of which have and may in the future result in a reduction in our fill rates to our customers.

components.reason: Enumerates multiple specific pandemic-related supply-chain vulnerabilities.
Links risks to reduced customer fill rates (sales impact).
Forward-looking language signals continued exposure.
Absence of quantified magnitude.
Event still recent.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Wide array of concrete supply-chain threats justifies a solid mid-high score.

evidence_list.snippet: As a result of academic and in-restaurant dining shutdowns during the COVID-19 pandemic, each of our segments previously experienced a shift in demand from foodservice to retail.

components.reason: Notes realised change in demand mix attributable to pandemic shutdowns.
Applies to ‘each of our segments’, indicating broad operational effect.
Past impact—unclear persistence lowers immediacy.
Recent timeframe preserves relevance.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows concrete historical demand shock but limited forward detail; moderate severity.

evidence_list.snippet: While each of our segments has subsequently experienced varying levels of foodservice recovery, the long-term impact of COVID-19 remains uncertain and will depend on a number of future developments, which are uncertain and cannot be predicted at this time.

components.reason: Admits uncertainty around long-term demand trajectory.
Covers all segments (broad scope).
Generic, non-quantified statement.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Uncertainty without detail yields a modest risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, in the event of a protracted period of economic downturn either in the near term or as a result of a future global pandemic, demand for our foodservice products may remain below expectations or decrease further, and demand for our retail consumption products may also decrease, which could have an adverse impact on our results of operations.

components.reason: Links pandemic-driven downturn to reduced demand and earnings impact.
Addresses both foodservice and retail channels.
Hypothetical and unquantified.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking demand risk across channels but no current impact, so mid-low score.

evidence_list.snippet: We also face other risks associated with or potentially originated from the COVID-19 pandemic, including: • additional increase in input cost may not be adequately captured through pricing; • adverse changes to the global economy may subject us to risk of material intangible and long-lived asset impairments, adjustments for inventory and market volatility for items subject to fair value measurements such as derivatives and investments; • an increase in working capital needs and/or an increase in trade accounts receivable write-offs (and associated reserves) as a result of increased financial pressures on our suppliers or customers who are not able to pay in a timely manner or at all; • a shift in consumer spending as a result of an economic downturn, which could result in consumers moving to private label or lower price products; and • litigation.

components.reason: Lists multiple concrete financial exposures (input cost capture, impairments, receivable write-offs, litigation).
Signals potential material impact on assets and liquidity.
Breadth of risks (pricing, accounting, consumer behaviour).
No dollar amounts provided.
Recent event window.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive catalogue of financial threats justifies a high score despite no quantification.

evidence_list.snippet: Actions taken by governmental authorities and other third parties in response to risks associated with COVID-19, or if in the event of a new global pandemic, are unknown and are impossible to predict with certainty.

components.reason: Highlights uncontrollable regulatory/policy uncertainty.
Emphasises unpredictability which complicates planning.
Generic, no direct impact quantified.
Still within recent time horizon.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Policy unpredictability adds risk but lack of specifics keeps score modest.

evidence_list.snippet: Nor can the Company predict whether or when a COVID-19 variant or widespread illness will or can disrupt our business in the future.

components.reason: States inability to forecast future variant disruption.
Generic uncertainty.
Recency keeps some weight.

evidence_list.snippet: Any such disruption could adversely impact our business and results of operations.

components.reason: Links disruption (e.g., pandemic) to adverse business impact.
Highly generic phrasing lowers informativeness.
Recent timeframe provides minimal extra weight.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Catch-all adverse-impact clause; minimal incremental information so low score.

evidence_list.snippet: The impact of COVID-19 pandemic, including any resurgence and new or existing variants, on the global economy and on consumer demand worldwide;

components.reason: Acknowledges pandemic’s worldwide economic and demand impact.
Extends risk to international operations and exports.
Bullet fragment, generic, no numbers.
Timeframe still recent.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Adds global-demand dimension but remains high-level; moderate score.
